title: Native prime-field factor-base size and decomposition-oracle tuning
status_note: Draft protocol written (PROTOCOL.md, DRAFT): frozen incumbent = frontier ic-pair (prime-abscissa + mitm:negation_folded=1, N 32/162/407/1024), 5-size x 5-oracle train grid on fresh prime_search curves, hash-frozen selection, 48-target x 2-round holdout per size, band-priced paired decision. Not frozen: needs ecbench compare --weight, then pin and record the blob. No experiment run or scheduled; sizing probes only (PROTOCOL.md section 11).
blocked_on: note: ecbench compare has no --weight option (src/bin/ecbench.rs:228 Compare; src/cryptanalysis/ecbench/compare.rs:288 compare) and band.rs:187 ranks means without intervals, so the paired cluster-bootstrap intervals at w=0.1 and w=1 required by PROTOCOL.md section 7.2 cannot be computed natively; run.sh analyse exits 3 until it lands

note: no seeded random prime factor-base plug-in (src/cryptanalysis/ecbench/methods.rs:2125-2137 admits prime-abscissa, prime-projected-abscissa, glv-orbit, prime-kummer, prime-isogeny, cm-scalar-orbit only); random-base control replaced by a stride control unless a prime-random plug-in lands before freezing (control gap, not the primary decision)
note: freeze steps pending: merge card files and the compare --weight change, pin code.commit to that merge, commit PROTOCOL.md as FROZEN and record protocol.blob (PROTOCOL.md section 12)
question: Can joint selection of factor-base size and exact native decomposition oracle reduce complete one-target IC cost against the current verified prime-field incumbent on fresh matched workloads?
decision_value: A verified holdout reduction robust to the common native-operation pricing band promotes the selected recipe to the next IC baseline, even if rho is still cheaper. A null, failed or price-sensitive result retains the incumbent and narrows the tuning question; no coverage-only result is promoted to a pipeline improvement.

resources.notes: Derived in README.md from measured per-run walls (frontier Phase 1 sessions; this card's probes A-C): ~50 min of one core for identity, train (+edge extensions), holdout, panel K, replay-all audit and analysis, plus ~20 min for outputs.verify; 2 core-hours / 2 wall-hours include ~2x margin for a contended spot host. Peak process RSS ~0.66 GiB (mitm m=3, N=4096, 32 bits); ~30 MB of session records. Estimates, not measurements.

outputs.result_schema: ecbench sessions (ecbench.record/v1) under {out}/sessions, replay-all receipts under {out}/audits, xp-pbo.selection/v1 + FROZEN.sha256 under {out}/select, ecbench.band/v1 and compare JSON under {out}/analysis (PROTOCOL.md section 13)

cairn.notes: Not published or leased; draft only. One sequential shard; resumable at session granularity by rerunning the same command (--resume).
